result.title: Personalized Federated Direct Preference Optimization via LoRA Adapters
result.comment: 15 pages, 11 figures, AAAI Fall Symposium Series 2026
result.summary: Federated Direct Preference Optimization (FedDPO) enables privacy-preserving alignment of language models across distributed agents without centralizing sensitive preference data. However, existing FedDPO analysis assumes all clients converge to a single shared policy, which is fundamentally at odds with the heterogeneous preference distributions present in practice. We propose Personalized FedDPO (pFedDPO), in which each client maintains a small private LoRA adapter atop a shared global base model. In pFedDPO, the base model is synchronized via FedAvg each round, while LoRA adapters remain local and capture client-specific preference patterns. We prove that this decomposition replaces the gradient diversity $κ^2$ in the FedDPO bound with a residual heterogeneity $κ^2_{\mathrm{eff}}$, which is no larger than $κ^2$ when adapters absorb client-specific directions, at the cost of an additive adapter-bias term that vanishes as adapters converge. Experiments on preference datasets show that pFedDPO consistently attains a lower gradient norm than vanilla FedDPO while remaining competitive in training loss and per-client reward accuracy.

AI.relevance_reason: 论文研究联邦式 DPO 的个性化问题：在共享基座模型上为每个客户端保留私有 LoRA 适配器，并给出把梯度多样性替换为残差异质性的收敛界分析；这属于分布式对齐优化，未涉及视觉/多模态推理的内部状态、证据使用或停止决策，共享基座与私有适配器的分解也过于泛化，难以形成可核查的 LVR 方法线索，故不入选。
